investigacion.base:
The current count is **19 countries**. That comes from the latest ECDC weekly report, week 42, published 16 October 2026. If no new country is added before 30 October, the question resolves to 19. The number can only go up, because it is a running total for the season.

**What the resolution source says now (wnv-weekly.ecdc.europa.eu, as of 20 Oct 2026)**
- The week 42 report was published on 16 October 2026, based on data submitted up until and including 14 October 2026. It says: "Since the beginning of the 2026 transmission season, and as at 14 October, 222 areas affected by West Nile virus (WNV) have been identified in 19 countries across Europe".
- Affected areas by country: Italy (70), France (28), Greece (25), Romania (24), the Netherlands (15), Serbia (10), Belgium (6), Bulgaria (6), Croatia (6), Germany (6), Spain (6), North Macedonia (5), Hungary (4), Kosovo* (4), Austria (3), Albania (2), Cyprus (1) and Slovenia (1). That snippet shows only 18 countries. Moldova seems to be the 19th, since it appears in the case list: Moldova (1 case of which 1 had an unknown place of infection).
- This week, 14 areas are reported as affected for the first time this season.
- The Metaculus FAQ only defines what counts as a "credible source" if the ECDC page goes down. It has no bearing on the number.

**How the count has grown in 2026 (from ECDC reports)**
- Late June: 2 countries, Italy and North Macedonia (as of 24 June)
- 10 September: 161 areas … in 15 countries
- 30 September: 202 areas … in 16 countries
- 7 October: 208 areas … in 18 countries
- 14 October: 222 areas in 19 countries

So 4 countries were added over the five weeks to mid-October, but the pace is slowing as the season ends.

**Context**
- This is a record season: As of 7 October 2026, EU countries have reported 1 715 locally acquired human cases of WNV infection, the highest number ever reported. ECDC also notes the virus is moving north, into Belgium and the Netherlands.
- For comparison from my own memory (not checked here), the previous highest count of countries was in the low 20s, in the 2018 and 2024 seasons. Late in a season, ECDC usually adds 0 or 1 country per week, often from cases reported late.

**Scheduled before resolution**
- ECDC said a map and table will be updated every Friday from now until November. That means a week 43 report on 23 October and a week 44 report on 30 October, which should be the resolving report, with data up to about 28 October.
- Countries not yet on the list that could plausibly be added include Slovakia, Czechia, Portugal, Türkiye, Montenegro, Bosnia, Ukraine and Poland. Moldova is already counted.

**Bottom line:** the status quo is 19. Two more weekly updates are due before resolution. The most likely outcomes are 19 to 21, with 19 or 20 the most likely. I found no prediction-market prices for this question.

criterios: This question resolves as the number of countries stated in the "Current situation" section of the ECDC West Nile Virus weekly surveillance report (https://wnv-weekly.ecdc.europa.eu/) in the first report published on or after 29 October 2026 — expected to be the report published on Friday 30 October 2026. That section reads "... areas affected by West Nile virus (WNV) have been identified in Y countries across Europe"; the question resolves to the integer Y stated there. For example, if the report states areas "have been identified in 20 countries across Europe", this resolves as 20.
letra_pequena: If no new report is published on or after 29 October 2026 but a report for the 2026 season remains available at the source, the most recent 2026-season report available as of 31 October 2026 is used. If the ECDC weekly report page is unavailable, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the ECDC figure for the same report will be used. If ECDC stops publishing the figure entirely for the 2026 season, the question is annulled.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 10 days, with the resolving report expected on 30 October 2026.  
(b) **If nothing changes:** 19 countries; the seasonal count cannot fall.  
(c) **If the recent trend continues:** Roughly 20–21 countries, though new-country additions may slow this late in the season.  
(d) **Experts and markets:** ECDC reports 19 so far and warns of continued spread northward. I have no reliable market forecast to add.  
(e) **Unexpected low scenario:** No further countries are reported, leaving the count at 19.  
(f) **Unexpected high scenario:** Delayed reports or infections in several previously unaffected countries lift it to 23 or more.

(a) **Time left:** About 10 days. Two more weekly reports are due: week 43 on 23 October and week 44 on 30 October, which resolves the question.

(b) **If nothing changed:** 19 countries.

(c) **If the current trend continued:** About 1 new country every 1–2 weeks lately (2 added in week 41, 1 in week 42). Since the season is fading, that points to roughly 20, possibly 21.

(d) **Experts and markets:** There is no market for this question. The research assistant expects 19–21, with 19 or 20 most likely. Late in a season, ECDC typically adds 0 or 1 country per week, often because of cases reported late.

(e) **Low-outcome scenario:** Cold weather ends transmission and no late-reported cases arrive from new countries. The count stays at 19, its floor.

(f) **High-outcome scenario:** Several countries report late or retrospective cases at once (for example Slovakia, Czechia, Portugal, Türkiye or Montenegro), or Moldova-style entries based only on case lists get counted. That could push the total to 22–23.

My rough probabilities are: 19 at about 45%, 20 at about 33%, 21 at about 15%, and 22 or more at about 7%. Because the outcome is a whole number but the percentiles must strictly increase, the lower values are offset by small fractions.
